description.value: Yama Cafe is a homestyle Japanese cafe in East Vancouver opened in 2017 by Tokyo-born chef Mitsuhiro Yamamura, whose cooking philosophy centres on Washoku — a UNESCO-recognized approach to Japanese food that prizes seasonal ingredients and respectful technique. The cafe serves rice bowls, Japanese baked goods (called 'moffins'), custom cakes, and an Omakase bento and dinner course under the Special menu. A touring cyclist will find a calm, neighbourhood atmosphere with several gluten-free and vegan menu options alongside alternative milks.

address.value: 2007 East Hastings St, Vancouver, BC V5T 1T9

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The website is fully accessible and provides strong evidence throughout. The menu page confirms multiple gluten-free and vegan items by label, and the About Us page explains the chef's background and UNESCO Washoku heritage angle. The Special menu references an 'Omakase bento,' confirming a packaged meal option; Skip TheDishes delivery is explicitly promoted. No cycling-specific amenities (bike rack, washrooms, Wi-Fi, charging, water refill) appear anywhere on the site or in OSM tags, so those fields remain null.
concerns: OSM record has no phone number; 604-428-6276 sourced from website only — contact_confirmed.phone set to null.
Bike parking, washroom access, and water refill availability are unconfirmed; the listing would benefit from an on-the-ground visit to verify these required criteria.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: Active, independently run Japanese cafe on East Hastings with confirmed food service, vegan and GF menu options, and a bento takeout offering — a practical and distinctive food stop for touring cyclists passing through East Vancouver.

Packed lunches.detail: Special menu lists 'Omakase bento' — a chef's-choice bento box that constitutes a packaged, portable meal

Vegetarian / vegan / GF.detail: Menu explicitly labels Vegan Bowl as 'Gluten Free / Vegan', Tuna Tataki Bowl and Pork Bowl as 'Gluten Free'; custom cakes available gluten-free on request; soy, almond, and oat milk offered as dairy alternatives
